name.ja: アーサー・コンプトン

overview.en: Arthur Compton was an American physicist who demonstrated that X-rays and gamma rays have particle-like properties through the Compton scattering effect. His work provided key evidence for the quantum nature of electromagnetic radiation. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1927.

early_life.en: Compton was born in Wooster, Ohio, into an academic family. He studied at the College of Wooster and Princeton University, earning his doctorate in 1916. He initially worked on X-ray scattering at Washington University in St. Louis.

impact.en: The Compton effect provided definitive evidence that light has particle properties, helping to establish wave-particle duality. His work was crucial in the acceptance of quantum mechanics. During World War II, he directed the Metallurgical Laboratory that contributed to the development of the first nuclear reactor.

event.en: Discovered the Compton effect, demonstrating photon-electron scattering.
Awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of the Compton effect.
Appointed director of the Metallurgical Laboratory for the Manhattan Project.
Oversaw the first nuclear chain reaction experiment under Enrico Fermi.
Served on the Interim Committee advising on the use of atomic weapons.

title.en: A Quantum Theory of the Scattering of X-Rays by Light Elements

description.en: Paper describing the Compton effect and providing evidence for the particle nature of light.
Comprehensive treatise on X-ray physics and electron interactions.

text.en: The scientist is not the person who always gives the right answers, but the one who asks the right questions.
